metadata.benchmark_federation: Karnataka Cooperative Milk Producers' Federation (KMF) - Brand Nandini
metadata.information_standard: Retail Milk Prices (Consumer Shelf Price / Packaged MRP)
metadata.unit_primary: Rs per kg Total Solids (Rs/kg TS)
metadata.verification_policy: Strictly verified government cabinet resolutions, KMF official notifications, NDDB, DAHD, IDA, and accredited national financial dailies. Zero synthetic estimations.

records.evidence: Following the November 1 revision, retail consumer prices for Nandini milk across all 15 district unions stabilized smoothly at Rs 54 per litre with healthy demand absorption and zero consumer pushback.
records.remarks: Retail price staircase stabilizes across all district milk unions under BAMUL, KMF Mother Dairy, and regional unions.

records.evidence: KMF management confirmed that Nandini retail milk prices will remain unchanged through the winter season as flush arrivals remain robust, maintaining retail stability at Rs 54 per litre.
records.remarks: Statutory retail price freeze held firm; winter flush volumes satisfy urban liquid consumption without retail margin stress.

records.evidence: Karnataka cooperative retail liquid milk prices remain firmly pegged at Rs 54/L. Although early summer temperature rise tightens raw collections in northern zones, administered MRP remains unchanged.
records.remarks: Administered retail price plateau. Transition into early summer dry period.

records.evidence: Summer lean demand for curd, buttermilk, and lassi surges across Bengaluru Urban and Mysuru. Despite elevated farmgate procurement costs, KMF statutory policy ensures retail milk prices remain locked at Rs 54/L.
records.remarks: Summer lean season surge in fermented dairy products; retail price ceiling maintained.

records.evidence: Peak summer lean period across Deccan plateau brings acute green fodder deficits. District cooperative unions manage margins via SMP conversion balances, keeping consumer retail milk prices steady at Rs 54/L.
records.remarks: Deep summer lean season peak; administered retail price stability intact.

records.evidence: Late summer dry conditions persist across Northern Karnataka; cooperative federations utilize powder reconstitution buffers to maintain urban supply, keeping Nandini retail milk prices flat at Rs 54/L.
records.remarks: Late summer lean season buffering; administered retail ceiling maintained.

records.evidence: Onset of the South-West Monsoon over coastal Karnataka and Malnad districts initiates pasture regeneration. KMF confirms retail prices will remain unchanged at Rs 54/L through the monsoon onset.
records.remarks: Monsoon onset provides initial green fodder relief; administered retail price stability intact.

records.evidence: Surging monsoon rains across southern and coastal milk sheds bring significant improvements in animal hydration and green fodder availability, boosting daily milk yields while retail MRP stays fixed at Rs 54/L.
records.remarks: Monsoon green fodder expansion restores herd productivity; retail prices held flat.

records.evidence: Monsoon flush expands daily procurement by +12% across BAMUL and Hassan milk unions. Ample milk supply satisfies urban demand, preserving consumer retail price stability at Rs 54/L.
records.remarks: South-West monsoon flush expansion; cooperative supply abundance locks retail rate.

records.evidence: Festive demand for Gowri-Ganesha festivals absorbs liquid milk surplus without price pressure. KMF maintains statutory price freeze at Rs 54/L approaching the one-year mark of the Nov-2026 revision.
records.remarks: Festive liquid milk demand met smoothly by flush procurement; retail price remains flat.

records.evidence: Completing 12 months since the November 2026 revision, KMF operations report robust cooperative financial health. Consumer retail rates for Nandini toned milk remain firmly held at Rs 54 per litre.
records.remarks: 12-month post-revision plateau completed; statutory pricing policy holds retail rate firm.

records.evidence: Exactly one year after the 2026 revision, KMF reports steady retail distribution at Rs 54/L. The cooperative board signals price stability through the onset of the 2027-28 winter flush.
records.remarks: Annual anniversary of price revision; retail rates maintained at Rs 54/L.

records.evidence: Entering month 13 post-revision, KMF initiates internal financial review of union procurement costs. Retail shelf prices remain anchored at Rs 54/L during peak winter flush collections.
records.remarks: Next potential statutory revision window opens; winter flush buffers retail ceiling.

records.evidence: New Year retail milk rates hold flat at Rs 54/L across Karnataka. District cooperative unions manage margins via surplus milk conversion into Skimmed Milk Powder and butter.
records.remarks: Administered stability continues into early 2028.

records.evidence: Transition to 2028 summer lean period; KMF maintains Rs 54/L consumer shelf rate while monitoring cattle feed and fodder price indices for upcoming budget review.
records.remarks: Pre-summer lean transition; retail rates steady.

records.evidence: Entering month 16 post-revision, summer heat stress lowers milk production in Hyderabad-Karnataka. Retail prices held firm at Rs 54/L under established government convention.
records.remarks: Historical 16-month revision horizon reached; price stability monitored.

records.evidence: Peak summer dry season; dairy farmer associations submit memorandum to KMF requesting procurement support. Consumer retail price held flat at Rs 54/L pending state cabinet evaluation.
records.remarks: Peak dry season; cooperative petitions for potential next revision cycle.

records.evidence: Completing 18 full months since the November 2026 hike, KMF concludes the 2026-28 retail pricing cycle with steady performance at Rs 54/L ahead of the 2028 monsoon onset.
records.remarks: 18-month statutory cycle completes; retail price steady at Rs 54/L.

records.evidence: Following the state cabinet revision effective November 1, 2026, Nandini toned milk establishes a rock-solid quarterly retail baseline of Rs 54/L (455.89 Rs/kg TS) across Karnataka throughout Dec 2026 – Feb 2027.
records.remarks: Post-revision retail baseline holds firm across all 31 districts.

records.evidence: Karnataka retail milk rates maintain a steady quarterly average of Rs 54/L throughout the Mar-May summer lean season. By established convention, KMF prevents back-to-back retail increases within a 12-month window.
records.remarks: Administered retail price plateau during the summer lean season.

records.evidence: Transition from summer lean to south-west monsoon flush maintains an uninterrupted quarterly retail ceiling of Rs 54/L across Karnataka. Restored green fodder buffers milk union collection costs.
records.remarks: Monsoon pasture emergence protects producer margins; consumer retail shelf price held fixed.

records.evidence: Full monsoon flush arrivals and kharif maize harvest create procurement abundance for dairy unions. KMF maintains retail price freeze at Rs 54/L closing out the full 12-month post-revision cycle.
records.remarks: Monsoon flush supply abundance locks retail rate at Rs 54/L through the one-year mark.

records.evidence: Entering month 13–15 post-revision, retail shelf prices remain firmly anchored at Rs 54/L during winter flush. The standard statutory window for cost audit opens, with price stability monitored against cumulative inflation.
records.remarks: Statutory review window opens; winter flush buffers retail price ceiling.

records.evidence: 16 to 18 months post-revision represents the historical threshold for potential staircase price revisions in Karnataka. Baseline retail MRP holds at Rs 54/L, while what-if simulation models cost-push trigger points.
records.remarks: Historical 16–18 month staircase revision horizon; baseline sticky at Rs 54/L.

extended_outlook.expected_change: Potential Statutory Revision Window (18–24 Month Interval)
extended_outlook.evidence: Historically, KMF and the Karnataka State Cabinet review retail consumer prices on an administered 12 to 18 month cycle. Having implemented the +Rs 8/L revision on November 1, 2026, the 18-month milestone is reached in May 2028. Beyond this horizon, sustained feed inflation would trigger the next discrete retail price adjustment.
extended_outlook.remarks: Administered staircase pricing indicates potential next revision after 18 months of sticky retail pricing.
